newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Euromark volatility drags along floor.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Euromark volatility drags along floor.

text.p: Implied volatility of Euromark options traded on LIFFE was bouncing along the bottom on Tuesday, after large-lot selling late last week drained volatility, traders said.
Traders said more than 30,000 lots of September straddles were sold off around the 96.75 strike on Friday, at vols down to 8.0 percent, which added to the generally weak tone in volatility.
However, traders said the volatility could not keep getting cheaper and cheaper forever, however stable the German interest rate outlook appears to be.

"A lot of people are long options and euromarks (futures)," said Ian Aubrey, head of futures and options sales at Yamaichi International (Europe) in London. "The market is looking vulnerable to the downside."
Traders said Euromark volatility has been on a downward trend since the beginning of the year, when it was around the 16.0 percent level.
September at-the-money call options on the September futures were trading around 8.5 percent, little changed from Monday. December volatility was at 12.6-12.7 percent, also little moved.
At 1423 GMT September Euromark futures were up 0.01 at 96.81, while December was up 0.02 at 96.72.

Germany last raised rates in mid-1992, and last cut rates in April 1996. The lombard is currently at 4.5 percent, while the discount rate is 2.5 percent. The repo rate of 3.0 percent has not been changed since August 1996.
Activity on the floor was focused on the September 97.00 calls, of which more than 1,500 had traded by 1400 GMT.
"Upside calls are attracting a lot of interest," said a trader at a British house. "Buying 97.00 even calls is a cheap punt."
He said there was a pronounced skew in out-of-the-money calls.
Aubrey said he advised selling out-of-the-money call volatility, and buying in-the-money put vol.
